sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiologic Framework
sections.content: Anisocoria is a pupillary size inequality >0.4mm. Clinically, it is categorized by the pupil that is 'abnormal' in light vs. dark conditions. A pupil that fails to constrict implies a parasympathetic (sphincter) defect (abnormal in light), while a pupil that fails to dilate implies a sympathetic (dilator) defect (abnormal in dark).

sections.title: The Anisocoria Diagnostic Algorithm
content: Step 1: Check pupillary reactions in bright and dim light.
Step 2: If anisocoria is greater in dim light, the smaller pupil is abnormal (Sympathetic/Horner's).
Step 3: If anisocoria is greater in bright light, the larger pupil is abnormal (Parasympathetic/CN III/Adie's).
Step 4: If equal in all lights, consider physiological anisocoria (up to 20% of population).

sections.title: Life-Threatening Horner's Syndrome Etiology
content: Carotid Artery Dissection (Painful Horner's + Neck/Head pain)
Pancoast Tumor (Apical lung mass compressing sympathetic chain)
Aortic Aneurysm (Disruption of thoracic sympathetic chain)
Brainstem Stroke (Wallenberg Syndrome - Lateral Medullary Infarction)
Cavernous Sinus Pathology (Mass effect or carotid-cavernous fistula)

content.explanation: P for Ptosis (Muller's muscle weakness), A for Anhidrosis (facial sweating loss), M for Miosis (sympathetic failure).

sections.title: Differential Diagnosis: Large Pupil (Mydriasis)
content: Third Nerve Palsy (Look for EOM involvement/Ptosis)

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always compare old photographs to rule out physiological anisocoria.
Painful Horner's syndrome is a medical emergency until carotid dissection is ruled out by CTA or MRA.
Light-near dissociation is pathognomonic for tonic pupil or Parinaud's syndrome.
Pharmacological miosis from pilocarpine can be identified by the 'pilocarpine test'—if the pupil doesn't constrict, it's likely fixed by iris synechiae or structural damage.

branches: 2nd Order: Lung Apex/Pleura to Superior Cervical Ganglion
3rd Order: Internal Carotid Plexus to Iris Dilator
